text: Git branching is a powerful tool that helps developers work on new features without disrupting the main codebase. Instead of making changes directly to the main branch, you create a feature branch, which is like a separate workspace. Here, you can experiment, fix bugs, or build new functionality safely. Once your work is ready, you create a pull request, which is a formal way to ask other team members to review your changes. After they approve it, you can merge the branch back into the main branch. This version control workflow keeps the project stable and organized, allowing multiple people to collaborate efficiently.
